messages:
deploy-bot: Deployed release v2.14.3 to canary cluster (canary-3) at 1765289001
maya: seeing p95 -> 220ms, p99 -> 1.1s on canary. Noticed error budget burn. dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/runtime/canary-3 (chart pinned)
sam: confirmed on SLO watch. Any notable config changes in this deploy?
jun: the diff included kernel selection tweak and batching heuristic update. Kernel switch: prefer 'optimized_matmul' over 'fused_attn' for medium seq-length. Batching: microbatch target bumped from 8 -> 16 for GPUs with high occupancy.
maya: profiler snapshots attached: high tail during generation step 2 (kv lookup). Looks like KV cache miss rate climbed to 18% from baseline 2%.
carla: @jun can you paste the exact kernel selection rule?
jun: snippet:
```
// kernel_priority order for canary
kernel_priority = ["optimized_matmul", "fused_attn", "aten_attn"]
// previous was ["fused_attn", "optimized_matmul"]
```
liam: kvcache miss spike + larger microbatches = tail amplification. If caches miss, you force more seq work per batch, and p99 explodes.
nisha: quick check: request size distribution on canary shifted — more short prompts suddenly, causing less kv reuse. Could be correlated with traffic seed change from experiments.
maya: I ran a heatmap trace of a single hot model: long stalls during kernel selection -> fallback path triggers additional memcpy. stack: kernel selector -> fallback -> aten path.
sam: ops-bot can we roll back the kernel order for canary? We need to stop SLO bleed.
ops-bot: Starting rollback: revert commit 8f3b2c (kernel-priority change) to canary-3. ETA ~2m
liam: also lowering microbatch target back to 8 on canary to reduce blocking. Command: `rictl set-config canary-3 batching.microbatch_target=8`
jun: ack. I'm reproducing locally with synthetic traffic to validate. If kernel priority was the root cause, p99 should drop quickly.
deploy-bot: Revert applied: commit 8f3b2c reverted at 1765289205. Canary traffic switching to previous config.
maya: charts look better already: p95 110ms, p99 260ms after revert. KV miss back to 3%. :tada:
carla: great. Can we capture a boiled-down repro? I think the combo of kernel ordering + larger microbatch amplifies rare misses. We should write a test that simulates random kv miss injection and measures tail across microbatch sizes.
sam: agree. Action items: 1) add regression test for kernel fallback tail, 2) add guard in rollout: if p99 increases >30% during canary, auto-pause, 3) investigate traffic seeding that increased short prompts.
nisha: I'll own test 1. jun will own patch to rollout guard. liam will follow up on autoscaler interplay.
maya: we should also log kernel fallback counts as a dedicated metric (runtime.kernel_fallback.count) and alert on >100/min per pool.
jun: noted. I'll open PRs for metrics + rollback playbook changes.
liam: one more note — packing heuristics: when microbatch_target is high, we rely on hot-KV locality to amortize kernel cost. With low locality, larger microbatches hurt tail. Add to postmortem.
carla: postmortem owner?
maya: I'll draft postmortem and include graphs + repro steps. Plan to add canary checklist: validate kv miss rate and kernel fallback before promoting.
sam: thanks all. Quick incident summary: deploy changed kernel priority + microbatch target -> increased kernel fallbacks and KV miss amplification -> p99 spike -> revert -> p99 recovered. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
